niche: a rail operating centre's signaller errors on its VDU workstations, where the local investigations book every wrong route to the signaller and the route's 2027 improvement plan funds one programme against the cause that accounted for the most operating-centre delay minutes
answer: B, the workstation display renewal, 8,985 delay minutes, delivery beginning on W03 Hatherby
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file correctly sums the operating centre's delay minutes by each local investigation's underlying cause and funds signaller competence training (programme A), or rates wrong routes per manual route request by signaller experience and by peak hour and funds the workload split (programme E), where the golden is the screen redraw (programme B), because the wrong routes at the routes whose two exit buttons sit eight to twelve pixels apart are slips onto the neighbouring exit that every signaller makes at the same rate.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each manual route-setting action's error probability taken apart by error mode, slips against mistakes, which human reliability analysis attributes to a design-induced performance shaping factor when the same slip recurs across operators at the same pair of controls; with another field's nouns there is no entrance-exit selection on a drawn schematic, so the pair geometry and the operators' own corrected slips that decide have no counterpart.
layer1: control system action log written by two servers, with both servers' copies around each server change
action log and ARS log in UTC against registers and rosters in UK local time across both clock changes
desk names renamed to W numbers and ARS sub-area codes renamed at release 8.2, on each server's own date
incident register moved to a new tool in April 2026, the old categories crosswalked by the tool's own sheet
delay attribution records with a review log moving minutes between incidents under three statuses
rosters in two layouts (a periodic grid with a code key, a long tool export) and a changes list missing changes made on the day
server B's ARS process stamping Central European time into the UTC column
the 2025-26 register's route text in three forms
stakeholder_role: the operating centre's safety and assurance manager, preparing the improvement plan the route's safety review panel commits for 2027

spine.entity: one signaller action the control system logged (route request, set, cancel, rejection)

world.org_type: rail infrastructure manager's regional operating centre

driver: The decisive quantity is which of the operators' wrong selections were slips onto the control drawn next to the intended one, read from the controls' drawn positions against each wrong selection's set and required target and from the operators' own quick reversals of the same slip, because the record books every wrong selection to the operator who made it and the error rates by operator experience, workload and hour each point to another cause.
driver_concrete: The wrong routes the local investigations book to signaller competence are, at the routes whose two exit buttons sit eight to twelve pixels apart on the workstation screens, slips onto the neighbouring exit that every signaller makes at the same rate in quiet and busy hours, read from the display data's button positions against each wrong route's set and required exit and from the control system's routes cancelled within seconds and reset from the same entrance; the screen redraw accounts for the most delay minutes, against competence training by the investigations' categories and the workload split by the peak-hour error rates.
stump: A competent solver sums the operating centre's delay minutes by each local investigation's underlying cause and funds signaller competence training (A), or rates wrong routes per manual request by experience and peak hour and funds the workload split (E), because no column marks a slip, the investigations book every wrong route to the signaller, and the drawn-close routes carry the peak hours' extra requests.

differentiation.task107: task107 v2 scales a lottery pilot's assignment effect for a comparison arm contaminated by staff reassigned from treated units, reached through a timetable, a staff directory and a certification register; task399 has no comparison arm or assignment: it separates each wrong route's error mode, a slip onto the exit drawn beside the one wanted against a decision error, by the screen positions of the two exits and the signallers' own routes cancelled and reset within seconds.
differentiation.task121: task121 v4 links each satisfaction response to the conditions of the passenger's journey because ratings carry a halo, and v6 builds each call-taker's rest from consecutive shifts; task399 reads no rating and no exposure built from a worker's own history: the decisive property is a fixed geometry of two controls on a screen, shared by every operator who uses them, read through the operators' corrected slips.
differentiation.task398: task398 routes a pollutant through a stratified lake to the one intake depth that draws a single tributary's layer, a physical attribution read from temperature profiles; task399 re-classifies operators' recorded errors as slips by the drawn geometry of two controls on a screen and the operators' own quick cancel-resets. They share the Root-Cause objective's ordinary labels (gap objective, decision root_cause_named) and no decisive rung, file role or data structure.

notes: Seed RC05's world (an electricity distributor's one reliability programme) is closed for this number: grid-reliability-outage-analysis holds seven cards and its slot notes spend auto-reclose completion (task198 H4), protection coordination (task129), shared substation supply (task303) and same-phase repeats (task192). The build keeps the seed's decision (one programme from a catalogue of five) and quantity (the outcome units the funded programme's cause accounted for over the last twelve months) and moves to Human Factors & Ergonomics under Root-Cause.
